sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_shifted: insert_after_residue 23 -> 42 on human canonical P26010 (paper numbering: ortholog:mouse (mature-protein numbering), construct species: mouse). Paper (PMID 32764635): "beta7 chains cDNA which were inserted PA tag into 4 locations (PAins 1: 23/24, PAins 2: 29/30, PAins 3: 427/428, PAins 4: 431/432) were introduced into BAF cells (Fig. 1b,c) ... All mutants of beta7 were approximately equally expressed on the cell surface (Fig. 1c). ... for PAins 1: 5'-CCTGACCTGTCTCTGCAGGGCGTTGCCATGCCAGGTGCCGAAGATGATGTGGTGGGATCCTGCCAGCCAGTT-3'". Audit note: Full text read from PMC7413538. The PAins1 inverse-PCR primer translates to ...PDLSLQ|GVAMPGARDDVV|GSCQPV..., i.e. the PA tag follows mouse Itgb7 (P26011) precursor Q42 = mature residue 23 after the 19-aa signal peptide. Mouse 42 aligns to human P26010 L42 (ATEWRNPHLSML|GSCQPAPSCQKC), offset 0, so the human insert_after is 42 (L|G), not 23 (A|K); the same +19 shift as the three training ITGB7 rows (29->48, 427->446, 431->450). Surface: NZ-1 and FIB504 flow cytometry on beta7-KO BAF cells show PAins1 at the surface; NZ-1 binding to PAins1 was conformation-independent (only PAins2 reports Mn2+ activation). Function (MAdCAM-1 binding) was measured on PAins2 cells only.] L2 explicitly names junction 23/24 (PAins1) in the N-terminal PSI domain segment of full-length membrane-anchored β7. Python confirms residue 23 = A and residue 24 = K in the canonical human sequence; both are extracellular (landmarks: EC 20–725) and >700 residues from the TM boundary. L3 confirms surface display by flow cytometry for all four insertion mutants including PAins1; ranked below PAins2 because the Mn2+-dependent conformational readout is not separately reported for this junction. Full-length murine β7 integrin expressed in β7-KO BAF cells via pcDNA3.1 construct; PA tag inserted between residues 23 and 24 (PAins1) by inverse PCR; surface display confirmed by NZ-1 (anti-PA) and FIB504 (anti-β7) flow cytometry in the presence of Ca2+/Mg2+ or Mn2+.

sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_shifted: insert_after_residue 29 -> 48 on human canonical P26010 (paper numbering: mature_protein, construct species: mouse). validation_level surface_and_function -> surface_only (paper reports surface: yes, function: not_reported). Paper (PMID 32764635): "PA tag into 4 locations (PAins 1: 23/24, PAins 2: 29/30, PAins 3: 427/428, PAins 4: 431/432) were introduced into BAF cells". Audit note: Construct is murine beta7 (pcDNA3.1-murine beta7, inverse PCR) and the paper's positions are mature-protein numbering: translating the PAins primers puts the PA tag after precursor residues 42, 48, 446 and 450 (signal peptide 19 aa). Mouse and human align with offset 0 in these regions, so the human canonical junction is 48 (GSCQPA|PSCQKC), not 29. All four mutants expressed on the cell surface by NZ-1/FIB504 flow cytometry. PAins2 reports Mn2+-dependent conformational change (NZ-1 binding up); ligand binding/adhesion of the tagged integrin not measured.] L2 explicitly names junction 29/30 (PAins2) in the N-terminal segment of the PSI domain of full-length membrane-anchored β7. Python confirms residue 29 = G and residue 30 = D in the canonical human sequence; both are extracellular (landmarks: EC 20–725) and >690 residues from the TM boundary. L4 provides the strongest functional validation of all four sites: Mn2+-dependent 8-fold increase in NZ-1 binding demonstrates that conformational regulation of α4β7 is intact with the tag at this position. Full-length murine β7 integrin expressed in β7-KO BAF cells (proB line) via pcDNA3.1 construct; PA tag inserted between residues 29 and 30 (PAins2) by inverse PCR; surface display confirmed by NZ-1 (anti-PA) flow cytometry; FIB504 (anti-β7, MAdCAM-1 binding-site epitope) staining also performed.

sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_shifted: insert_after_residue 427 -> 446 on human canonical P26010 (paper numbering: mature_protein, construct species: mouse). Paper (PMID 32764635): "PA tag into 4 locations (PAins 1: 23/24, PAins 2: 29/30, PAins 3: 427/428, PAins 4: 431/432) were introduced into BAF cells". Audit note: Construct is murine beta7 (pcDNA3.1-murine beta7, inverse PCR) and the paper's positions are mature-protein numbering: translating the PAins primers puts the PA tag after precursor residues 42, 48, 446 and 450 (signal peptide 19 aa). Mouse and human align with offset 0 in these regions, so the human canonical junction is 446 (VSLQAT|HCLPEP), not 427. All four mutants expressed on the cell surface by NZ-1/FIB504 flow cytometry. The row's claim that the tag sits before a PSI-domain cysteine C428 is an artefact of the numbering error.] L2 explicitly names junction 427/428 (PAins3) in the C-terminal PSI domain segment of full-length membrane-anchored β7. Python confirms residue 427 = Q and residue 428 = C in the canonical human sequence; both are extracellular (landmarks: EC 20–725) and ~299 residues from the TM boundary. The tag is inserted immediately before C428, a disulfide-bonded cysteine of the PSI domain; the paper reports this insertion as functional (surface display confirmed), so the disulfide network is apparently tolerant of the upstream insertion, but this proximity to a structural cysteine warrants caution and lowers confidence relative to PAins4. Full-length murine β7 integrin expressed in β7-KO BAF cells via pcDNA3.1 construct; PA tag inserted between residues 427 and 428 (PAins3) by inverse PCR in the C-terminal PSI domain segment; surface display confirmed by NZ-1 (anti-PA) and FIB504 (anti-β7) flow cytometry.
